hadith:
Belief - Narrated 'Aisha:

Once the Prophet (ﷺ) came while a woman was sitting with me. He said, "Who is she?" I replied, "She is so and so," and told him about her (excessive) praying. He said disapprovingly, "Do (good) deeds which is within your capacity (without being overtaxed) as Allah does not get tired (of giving rewards) but (surely) you will get tired and the best deed (act of Worship) in the sight of Allah is that which is done regularly."
message: Allah's infinite nature—Al Waasi', the All-Encompassing—reminds us that His mercy and provisions extend beyond what we can comprehend, yet we often exhaust ourselves through excessive striving. The Prophet (ﷺ) taught us that consistent, sustainable good deeds done within our capacity are more beloved to Allah than overwhelming ourselves, for He never tires of rewarding us while we tire ourselves. Let this be a gentle reminder to balance your spiritual journey with wisdom and moderation, trusting in Allah's vast support.
name:
Al Waasi' - الْوَاسِعُ - The All-Encompassing

This name reflects Allah's infinite nature, His ability to encompass all things within His knowledge, mercy, and power. It signifies that Allah's provisions and knowledge extend beyond human comprehension and limitations, offering reassurance of His omnipresence and support in the lives of His creations.
verse:
An-Nazi'at - Those who drag forth - 79:29

He dimmed its night, and brought forth its daylight.
